Front Page · Custody & Markets

Every Loss This Week Needed Someone Else’s Key

A $12 million bridge drain, a Nasdaq-listed ether loan without a human negotiator, and sovereign gold flights all land on the same seam: the moment an asset’s control crosses to another party’s signature.

Compiled from reports by Roger, TFTC, markusturm, and bitcoin.rocks

On Saturday, bitcoin touched $55,130—its lowest mark since September 2024 and roughly 56 percent below its October 2025 high—before snapping back 9 percent above $60,000 and settling near $58,900 to $59,700 by Sunday morning [s530] [s544]. The bounce marked day 411 since the 2025 peak, making the drawdown one day longer than the post-halving trough cited by Blocktrainer, and arrived on the fourth anniversary of the November 21, 2022 low near $15,500 after FTX collapsed [s530] [s153].

Yet the weekend’s sharpest argument is that price swings and custody failures are separate events [s544]. While $1.8 billion in leveraged positions—$1.3 billion of them longs—were cleared out in 24 hours and seven-day realised losses crossed $11.3 billion, an estimated $12 million exit at cross-chain swap protocol Chainflip could not be reversed by a rally [s530] [s543] [s544]. An attacker funded preparation through Tornado Cash on November 11, registered a malicious validator on November 20, and compromised the threshold signing key to drain 122.86 BTC, 520.22 ETH, 3.25 million USDC, and 758,141 USDT on Saturday [s543] [s544]. With deposits and swaps halted in full safe mode, Chainflip offered a 10 percent white-hat bounty—roughly $1.2 million—if 90 percent is returned by 18:38 UTC Monday [s543].

A custody failure is a change of ownership, and it does not come back when the chart recovers.

Two days earlier, Nasdaq-listed BTCS disclosed in an SEC filing that it held about $54 million in stablecoin debt on Aave against 46,676 ETH, leaving its modelled liquidation point near $1,450 after ether hit $1,536 on Saturday [s544]. As Roger observed of the filing, We can provide no assurance as to the future amount of our borrowings, the value of our collateral, or that a liquidation will not occur. [s544] Meanwhile, an OMFIF working-group report drawn from eight central banks found reserve managers moving physical gold back into domestic vaults—including roughly 86 tonnes shifted by De Nederlandsche Bank and 129 tonnes replaced in Paris by the Banque de France—because assets held in foreign custody carry freezing risk [s542] [s544].

From inside the bear-market gloom, Théo Mogenet of Bull Bitcoin argued that too many cycle entrants came for price action rather than the underlying fiscal math of sovereign debt traps [s540]. And in Chiang Mai, Alex Li offered a ground-level reminder of fee incentives at a weekend market: Thai vendors turned down Visa and Mastercard over ~5 percent charges while accepting Alipay and WeChat Pay at zero fee [s226].

Protocol & Security Briefs

P2Pool V2 Runs on Testnet5 as Devs Probe Multisig Setup

Decentralized mining payouts, BIP 54 edge cases, and a zero-server key-exchange draft led the technical weekend.

Bitcoin’s new Testnet5—activated at block 975,744 under BIP 95—is now carrying steady hashrate for P2Pool V2, testing decentralized sharechain payouts ahead of Tuesday’s developer AMA [s528] [s530]. On Delving Bitcoin, developer onedigitmoney proposed a Multisig Session Protocol so cosigners can verify a twelve-character code out of band instead of trusting an email or server relay during setup, while Antoine Riard examined a narrow timestamp edge case in BIP 54 [s530]. Separately, Ben Weeks flagged a Coinos v3 API name-claim issue affecting one-tap Lightning Piggy family wallets [s131].

Software, Local AI & Open Protocols

Sunday Bench · Tools & Infrastructure
Local Inference

Apple Silicon Engines Tested on a 96 GB MacBook

Juraj

Benchmarking local language models on a 96 GB M2 Max MacBook, Juraj reported that the inference engine matters roughly as much as the weights [s375]. Native engine MTPLX ran 1.3 times faster than Ollama’s MLX runner on a mixture-of-experts model and 1.7 times faster on a dense 27B model by drafting tokens ahead with multi-token prediction heads [s375]. For oversized weights that outgrow memory, he turned to antirez’s DwarfStar (ds4), streaming a 95 GB n-gram table off SSD while holding 42 GB in RAM [s375].

Elsewhere in self-hosted tooling, Sirius Lightning detached a Roborock Qrevo vacuum from vendor cloud servers using a local Python server and Pi-hole DNS routing [s291] [s303], while Max Trotter and franzap debated where LLM coding helpers hallucinate complexity versus nail data-wrangling scripts [s8] [s160].

Kemal, Gigi, hzrd149, Dawn, Cruz

Kemal shared a Scientific American report that mathematician Alpöge claims a proof of the Riemann hypothesis, noting what a confirmed proof means: prime numbers remain deterministic while behaving like a coin-flip random walk [s308] [s310].

Culture & Long-Form

Patagonia Trails, Alberta Turnarounds, and a Phoenix Loft

Travelsats, sey, West Major, Gunnar Stødle, Avis

Long-form writers ranged far past the charts. Travelsats filed a three-day trail guide to Villa La Angostura in Patagonia, noting Sunday’s Gran Fondo bike-race closure on the Seven Lakes road from 6 a.m. to noon [s536]. Under a boilermaker persona, sey chronicled how shifting two- and four-year industrial maintenance schedules in Alberta’s oil sands cut turnaround income from roughly $144,000 to $59,000 [s535].

Closer to the bench, West Major shared a photo tour of moving his apparel shop out of a spare apartment bedroom into an upstairs space in downtown Phoenix [s290].
